newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government seeks debate on pension funds.
newsitem.headline: French government seeks debate on pension funds.

text.p: The French government is open to discussion with interested parties on whether pension funds due to be introduced to France should make payouts in annuities or a lump sum, government officials said on Tuesday.
A draft bill on pension funds drawn up by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis had suggested these should pay out money in annuities only.
However Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Monday that the idea of pension funds paying out money in a lump sum could be considered.

"At retirement age, one could have an annuity which improved the basic pension...or otherwise -- I am not completely opposed to this idea -- a lump sum which for example would allow someone who is retiring to sell their appartment in town in order to by a retirement house in the country," Juppe said on French radio.
French banks have pushed for pension funds to pay out money in a lump sum, whereas insurance companies which would prefer the payout to be in the form of annuities.
The National Assembly is expected to debate a bill on pension funds in the autumn, while Arthuis said in July he expected these to be in place by the start of next year.

The tax regime for the new pension funds is due to be included in the 1997 budget which will be presented on September 18. It is likely to make contributions to pension funds tax deductible, while payouts would be taxable.
